title: Machine Learning Approaches for Mental Illness Detection on Social Media: A Systematic Review of Biases and Methodological Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the distribution of social media platforms (e.g., Twitter, Reddit, Facebook) used for data collection across 47 reviewed studies to identify overreliance on specific networks.

Evaluating the sampling techniques used in the primary studies, such as keyword filtering, convenience sampling via APIs, and reliance on crowdsourcing platforms like MTurk, to identify exclusion of specific user behaviors and demographic profiles.
Quantifying the proportion of studies focusing exclusively on English-language content versus non-English languages to assess linguistic representativeness.
Reviewing the reported geographical origins of the social media data to identify the overrepresentation of users from specific regions, particularly the United States and Europe.

Using the PROBAST (Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool) framework to systematically assess flaws across the machine learning lifecycle, including data preprocessing (e.g., handling negative words), model development (e.g., hyperparameter tuning, data partitioning), and evaluation (e.g., handling class imbalance).
